full_judgment:
Chowdhury A.T.M. Masud J.-This appeal by special leave arises out of the judgment and order dated 19-5-82 of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 43 of 1982 affirming those dated 18-1-82 of the Sessions Judge, Bogra, in Sessions Case No. 448 of 1981, arising out of Khetlal P.S. Case No. 5(5) of 1980 and G.R. Case No. 155 of 1980 under sections 302/380 of the Penal Code, pending in the Court of Sessions Judge, Bogra. 

 The prosecution case in short is that while the complainant's brother, his Bhabi and nephews were sleeping in the first floor of their house, some miscreants entered the house on the night of 14-5-80 at about 2/3 a.m. and while they were taking away two bi-cycles from the ground floor of the house, brother of the complainant, his Bhabi and nephew caught hold of one of the miscreants and at that time another miscreant fired gun shot, as a result thereof the complainant's brother, his Bhabi and nephew succumbed to the gun shot injuries. 

 2. The defence case is that the accused persons are innocent and close relations of the deceased and that they have been falsely implicated in the case out of enmity and that they were not mentioned in the First Information Report as accused. 

 4. Appellants prayer for bail was rejected by the Sessions Judge, Bogra. Thereafter they moved the High Court Division for bail and obtained a Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 43 of 1982, which was subsequently discharged on 19-5-82. Against the saidorder the appellants moved this Court and obtained special leave to appeal. 

 5. Mr. Abdul Malek Ukil, the learned Counsel, appearing for the appellants submits that there is no allegation of any overt act against the appellants in the First Information Report and that they have been falsely implicated in the case out of enmity. He further submits that appellant No.1 is suffering from various diseases and is lying in Bogra hospital for treatment and that appellant No.2 is an old man of 75 years of age and both of them are close relations of the deceased persons. It is submitted that co-accused Mustafizur Rahman who is alleged to have fired the fatal gunshot was granted bail on 23-1-82 by the Sessions Judge, Bogra, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 448 of 1981 and further the High Court Division granted bail to another co-accused Jinnah Rahman on 30-10-81 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 141 of 1981. 

 6. Mr. Ukil, argues that there was no material to discriminate the cases of the appellants from those of the aforesaid co-accused and the learned judges of the High Court Division did not take into consideration all the materials relevant for granting bail to the appellants. Mr. AW. Bhuyan, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the State argues that names of the appellants were mentioned in the First Information Report as persons present at the time and place of occurrence and police having found prima facie case against them submitted charge- sheet under section 302 of the Penal Code and as such their prayer for bail has rightly been rejected by the High Court Division. 

 7. The learned Additional Attorney-General could not however refute the contention of the learned Counsel for the appellants to the effect that one of the co-accused, namely, Mastafim Rahmq who is alleged to have fired the fatal gunshot has already been granted bail by the Sessions Judge and that another co-accused Jinnan Rahman has been granted bail by the High Court Division. We find no materials for which the cases of the appellants might be discriminated. Although granting of bail is a matter of discretion of tile Court concerned but having considered the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of opinion that the High Court Division has, not exercised its discretion judicially in rejecting the appellants prayer for bail.
